mainTopic: רבי אחאי's vessel and his agents; whether telling an agent הולך ('deliver') works like זכי ('acquire') when the recipient or sender dies.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבי אחאי's vessel. His two agents, רבי דוסתאי and רבי יוסי בר כיפר, disagree about returning it to the people who handed it over. רבי דוסתאי gives in because those people were frightening and dangerous, and רבי אחאי rules that he acted well. The גמרא then turns to a new topic: a sender tells an agent 'הולך,' deliver a מנה to someone, but the recipient has died. Two ברייתות disagree about whether the money goes back to the sender or to the recipient's heirs. רבי אבא בר ממל, רב זביד and רב פפא each settle the contradiction without saying הולך is like זכי. The גמרא then asks whether תנאים argue about הולך and זכי, and it reads a long ברייתא with many opinions that way. It rejects this proof by placing the ברייתא in the case of a שכיב מרע, which follows the argument between רבי אלעזר and the חכמים. It quotes that משנה, and the חכמים's story about the mother of the בני רוכל continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אחאי sends two agents to bring his vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחאי asks רבי דוסתאי בר רבי ינאי and רבי יוסי בר כיפר to bring his vessel back with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי אחאי) said to רבי דוסתאי בר רבי ינאי and to רבי יוסי בר כיפר: When you come back, bring it to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins. רבי אחאי makes the two חכמים his agents to bring his vessel to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the whole case. These two are acting as agents for the owner, רבי אחאי, and that is what makes the later argument possible: once the vessel is in their hands, is it already considered in the owner's hands?

keyTerms.meaning: When you come (on your way back)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ לְרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בַּר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
phrases.english: He said to Rabbi Dostai bar Rabbi Yannai
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אחאי, the owner of the vessel from the lines just before this.

phrases.english: and to Rabbi Yosei bar Keifar:
When you come back, bring it to me.
phrases.notes: "It" is his vessel, which was being held in נהרדעא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ לְרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בַּר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי אחאי's vessel from earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אחאי appoints two agents to bring his vessel to him.

steps.title: The holders hand over the vessel, then want it back
steps.stepSummary: The vessel is given to the agents. The givers ask the agents to make a קנין and take responsibility. The agents refuse, so the givers ask for the vessel back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went, and the people gave it to them. The people said: Let us make a קנין with you. The agents said: No. The people said: Then give it back to us.
steps.whatsHappening: The vessel is handed over, but the givers do not want to stay responsible for it on the way. When the agents refuse to take on responsibility with a קנין, the givers demand it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The givers wanted the agents to formally take responsibility for the vessel from that moment on. Without that, they felt they were still responsible, so they wanted to cancel the handover. This raises the question: once it reached the owner's agents, can the givers still take it back?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us make a קנין (formal act of acquisition) with you
A formal act that makes a transfer or obligation binding

phrases.english: They went, and they gave it to them.
They said to them: Let us make a formal acquisition with you;
phrases.notes: They mean: do a קנין so that you two become responsible for the vessel from now on.

phrases.english: They said to them: No.
They said to them: Then give it back to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזוּל, יַהֲבֵיהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the agents receive the vessel and a dispute begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The givers demand the vessel back after the agents refuse to take responsibility with a קנין.

steps.title: The two agents disagree about returning it
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי agrees to give the vessel back. רבי יוסי בר כיפר refuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי בר רבי ינאי said to them: Yes. רבי יוסי בר כיפר said to them: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The two agents split. One is willing to return the vessel, and the other refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר כיפר holds that once the vessel reached the owner's agents, the givers no longer have the right to take it back. רבי דוסתאי says yes, and the next steps show his reason was fear of these people.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי דוסתאי's 'yes' was a ruling about the law. Later he explains that he said yes out of fear for his life; the text does not tell us his view of the law.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִין;
phrases.english: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai, said to them: Yes;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר כֵּיפַר אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Keifar said to them: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The agents answer the givers' demand from step 2, and they disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסתאי agrees to return the vessel; רבי יוסי בר כיפר refuses.

steps.title: רבי יוסי is tormented and רבי דוסתאי says to hit him
steps.stepSummary: The people torment רבי יוסי בר כיפר. He asks רבי דוסתאי for help, but רבי דוסתאי tells them, 'Good, hit him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They were tormenting him. He said to him: See, Master, how they are acting! He said to them: Good, hit him.
steps.whatsHappening: The people pressure רבי יוסי בר כיפר by hurting him. Instead of defending him, רבי דוסתאי encourages them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shocking reaction sets up the question in the next step. The reader is left wondering why a חכם would encourage people to hit his colleague, and the answer comes at the end.

phrases.english: They were tormenting him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יוסי בר כיפר, the one who refused to give it back.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מָר הֵיכִי קָא עָבֵיד!
phrases.english: He said to him: See, Master, how they are acting!
He said to them: Good, hit him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲווֹ קָא מְצַעֲרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened after רבי יוסי בר כיפר refused.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי דוסתאי sides with the people against his colleague.

steps.title: רבי יוסי complains and רבי אחאי asks why
steps.stepSummary: Back with רבי אחאי, רבי יוסי בר כיפר complains about רבי דוסתאי. רבי אחאי asks רבי דוסתאי why he acted this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to him, he said: See, Master, not only did he not help me, he even told them, 'Good, hit him'! He (רבי אחאי) said to him (רבי דוסתאי): Why would you do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The agents return to רבי אחאי and the complaint is made. רבי אחאי asks רבי דוסתאי to explain himself, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי stresses two problems: רבי דוסתאי did not support him, and he even encouraged the people. רבי אחאי's question asks for the reason behind this strange behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only (literally: it was not enough for him)

phrases.english: When they came to him,
he said to him: See, Master,
not only did he not help me,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲמַר לְהוּ נָמֵי ״טָב רְמוֹ לֵיהּ״!
phrases.english: but he even said to them, 'Good, hit him'!
He said to him: Why would you do this?
phrases.notes: Here רבי אחאי is turning to רבי דוסתאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתוֹ לְגַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the event of step 4 to רבי אחאי and asks for a reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי דוסתאי encourage the people to hit his colleague?

steps.title: רבי דוסתאי explains he feared for his life
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי describes the people as strange and dangerous, ready to tie up or kill on command. He did not want to be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Those people are a cubit tall, their hats are a cubit, they speak from their middle, and their names are frightening: ארדא, ארטא, and פילי בריש. Tell them 'tie him up' and they tie up; tell them 'kill' and they kill. Had they killed דוסתאי, who would give my father ינאי a son like me?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי answers רבי אחאי's question. He explains that the people were dangerous, so he went along with them to save his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His behavior was not about the law of returning the vessel, but about danger. He describes how frightening they looked and how ready they were to harm or kill, and ends by saying his life was too precious to risk.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי דוסתאי's 'yes' and his 'hit him' came from fear of danger, not from a different view of the law. רבי יוסי בר כיפר's refusal is the position that stayed firm on the law.

phrases.english: He said to him: Those people —
they are a cubit tall, and their hats are a cubit,
and they speak from their middles,
and their names are frightening:
'Arda' and 'Arta' and 'Pili Bereish';
if they are told 'Tie him up,' they tie up;
if they are told 'Kill,' they kill;
had they killed Dostai,
phrases.notes: He is talking about himself, using his own name.

phrases.aramaic: מִי נָתַן לְיַנַּאי אַבָּא בַּר כְּמוֹתִי.
phrases.english: who would have given Yannai my father a son like me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹתָן בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אחאי's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי דוסתאי went along with the people because they were dangerous and he feared being killed.

steps.title: רבי אחאי checks how powerful those people were
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחאי asks רבי דוסתאי whether the people were close to the government and had followers ready to act. רבי דוסתאי answers yes to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: Are these people close to the government? He said: Yes. Do they have horses and mules running after them? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחאי asks two short questions to find out how dangerous the people really were. This sets up his ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחאי wants to confirm the danger before he judges רבי דוסתאי. Government connections and many followers mean the people could really harm someone, so refusing them was not a realistic option.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to the government, with political power
Horses and mules, a sign of wealth and servants

phrases.english: He said to him: These people,
are they close to the government?
He said to him: Yes.
Do they have horses and mules
that run after them?
phrases.notes: He means: do they have servants and followers ready to carry out their orders?

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי אָדָם הַלָּלוּ קְרוֹבִים לַמַּלְכוּת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי דוסתאי's explanation by checking the facts about the danger.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the people had real power, through government ties and followers, to carry out violence.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes to both. They were close to the government and had followers.

steps.title: רבי אחאי rules that רבי דוסתאי acted correctly
steps.stepSummary: Since the people were powerful and dangerous, רבי אחאי tells רבי דוסתאי that he did the right thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, you acted well.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחאי gives his verdict: given the danger, רבי דוסתאי behaved correctly. This ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the danger was real, רבי דוסתאי was right to protect his own life and not resist. רבי יוסי בר כיפר's complaint is therefore rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with רבי דוסתאי's behavior approved, because his life was truly in danger.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
you acted well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי שַׁפִּיר עֲבַדְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the verdict from the facts confirmed in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי דוסתאי acted properly by giving in to dangerous, powerful people.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about money sent to someone who could not be found
steps.stepSummary: A person told an agent to deliver a מנה to someone, but that person could not be found. One ברייתא says the money returns to the sender. Another says it goes to the recipient's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Deliver a מנה to so-and-so," and the agent went, looked for him, and did not find him. One ברייתא teaches: return it to the sender. Another ברייתא teaches: give it to the heirs of the person it was sent to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by presenting two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. The next steps will try to resolve the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the recipient already owned the money before he died. If he did, it belongs to his heirs. If he did not, it still belongs to the sender.

keyTerms.meaning: "Deliver" or "bring", an instruction to an agent
A sum of one hundred דינרים
One ברייתא teaches... and another ברייתא teaches

steps.confusionAlert: "Did not find him" here means the recipient had died. That is why his heirs come into the picture.

phrases.english: "Deliver a maneh to so-and-so,"
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred דינרים.

phrases.english: and he went and searched for him and did not find him,
phrases.notes: The person had died, which is why heirs are mentioned next.

phrases.english: one teaching says: it should go back to the sender;
and another teaching says:
to the heirs of the one it was sent to.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא יַחְזְרוּ לַמְשַׁלֵּחַ וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ לְיוֹרְשֵׁי מִי שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּלְחוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and opens a new legal discussion about the word הולך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on where undelivered money goes after the recipient dies.

steps.title: Suggestion that the teachings argue over whether 'deliver' means 'acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two ברייתות disagree about whether saying הולך works like saying זכי, which would make the agent acquire the money for the recipient right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about this: one master holds "deliver" is like "acquire," and the other holds "deliver" is not like "acquire"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a way to explain the contradiction: the two ברייתות hold different views on the meaning of הולך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הולך is like זכי, the agent acquired the money for the recipient immediately, so it goes to his heirs. If הולך is not like זכי, the recipient never owned it, so it returns to the sender.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say they argue about this?
"Acquire", meaning the agent takes ownership for the recipient right away

phrases.english: Shall we say that they argue about this:
one master holds "deliver" is like "acquire,"
phrases.notes: This would be the ברייתא that sends the money to the heirs.

phrases.english: and the other master holds "deliver" is not like "acquire"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a reason for the contradiction presented in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the contradiction into a dispute between two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to contradict each other with no explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: they disagree about whether הולך is like זכי.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר ממל: everyone agrees הולך is not זכי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל rejects the suggestion. Both ברייתות agree that הולך is not like זכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said: Everyone agrees that "deliver" is not like "acquire."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל pushes back on the גמרא's suggestion. There is no dispute about the meaning of הולך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both ברייתות agree that הולך does not make the agent acquire for the recipient, then that cannot be what they argue about. A different explanation is needed, and it comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
Everyone agrees that "deliver" is not like "acquire";

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הוֹלֵךְ לָאו כִּזְכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 10 that the ברייתות disagree about הולך.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the ברייתות argue over whether הולך is like זכי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no dispute here. Everyone holds that הולך is not like זכי.

steps.title: One teaching is about a healthy giver, the other about a dying giver
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל explains that the ברייתא saying "return to the sender" is about a healthy giver. The ברייתא saying "give to the heirs" is about a שכיב מרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not difficult: this ברייתא is about a healthy person, and that ברייתא is about a person on his deathbed.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first explanation, רבי אבא בר ממל resolves the contradiction a new way: the two ברייתות describe different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy person's gift is acquired only when it reaches the recipient, so if the recipient died first, the money returns to the sender. A שכיב מרע's gift is acquired right away, so the recipient already owned it and his heirs inherit it.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees הולך is not like זכי. The difference between the ברייתות is the giver: a healthy giver's money returns to him, but a שכיב מרע's gift goes to the recipient's heirs.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the special rules for a שכיב מרע's gift can change the outcome even when the agent never acquired the money for the recipient.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
this is about a healthy person,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא that sends the money back to the sender.

phrases.english: that is about a person on his deathbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּבָרִיא הָא בִּשְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the new resolution after step 11 rejected the first one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא describes a different giver
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות disagree about whether הולך is like זכי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree הולך is not like זכי. A healthy giver's money returns to him, while a שכיב מרע's gift goes to the recipient's heirs.

steps.title: רב זביד: both ברייתות are about a dying giver
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says both ברייתות are about a שכיב מרע. The difference is whether the recipient was alive when the money was handed to the agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Both ברייתות are about a person on his deathbed. One is where the recipient was alive when the money was given. The other is where the recipient was no longer alive when the money was given.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד offers a different way to settle the two ברייתות, still keeping the idea that הולך is not like זכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift from a שכיב מרע takes effect right away. If the recipient was alive at the moment the money was handed over, he owned it, so his heirs get it. If he was already dead at that moment, nobody could acquire it for him, so the money goes back to the sender.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one (both ברייתות)
He is there (alive) / he is not there (not alive)
The giving of the money (to the agent)

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
This one and that one are both about a person on his deathbed;
this one is where the recipient was alive
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says to give the money to the recipient's heirs.

phrases.english: at the time the money was given,
that one is where the recipient was not alive
at the time the money was given.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בִּשְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רבי אבא בר ממל's in step 12 to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: whether the recipient was alive when the money was handed over
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree, or they differ by whether the giver was healthy or dying.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about a dying giver. The ruling depends on whether the recipient was alive at the moment the money was given.

steps.title: רב פפא: both ברייתות are about a healthy giver
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says both ברייתות are about a healthy giver. The difference is who died first, the recipient or the giver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Both are about a healthy person. One is where the recipient died while the giver was still alive. The other is where the giver died while the recipient was still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a third way to settle the two ברייתות. He looks at who died first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the recipient died first, he never acquired the money, so it goes back to the sender. If the giver died first, there is a מצוה to carry out a dead person's wishes, so the recipient and his heirs get it. Here too, הולך is not treated like זכי.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This one and that one are both about a healthy person;
this one is where the recipient died in the giver's lifetime,
phrases.notes: This matches the ברייתא that says to return the money to the sender.

phrases.english: that one is where the giver died in the recipient's lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא בְּבָרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the same contradiction, different from those in steps 12 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: which person died first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות disagree, or the difference is about a dying giver.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about a healthy giver. If the recipient died first, the money returns to the sender. If the giver died first, it goes to the recipient's side.
steps.whatToRemember: Three אמוראים (רבי אבא בר ממל, רב זביד, רב פפא) all settle the two ברייתות without saying הולך is like זכי. Each uses a different split of the cases.

steps.title: Is this an argument among the תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that whether הולך works like זכי may be an argument among the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that whether "Deliver" is like "Acquire" is an argument among the תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new suggestion and is setting up the ברייתא it will bring next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא tried to explain the two ברייתות as arguing about הולך and זכי, and that idea was pushed away. Now it asks whether a different ברייתא shows that תנאים really do argue about this point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument among the תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that "Deliver" being like "Acquire"
is an argument among the תנאים?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא ״הוֹלֵךְ״ כִּ״זְכִי״ תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the two ברייתות, the גמרא opens a new question that goes back to the idea from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do תנאים actually argue about whether הולך works like זכי?

steps.title: The ברייתא: the sender died before the money was delivered
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: the agent could not find the recipient, so the money goes back to the sender. If the sender died, some say it goes to his heirs and some say it goes to the recipient's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "Deliver a מנה to so-and-so." The agent went and looked for him but did not find him. The money should go back to the sender. If the sender died, רבי נתן and רבי יעקב said it goes back to the sender's heirs. Some say it goes to the heirs of the one it was sent to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that seems to show an argument among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning the money to the sender's heirs fits the view that הולך is not like זכי, since the recipient never acquired it. Giving it to the recipient's heirs looks like the view that הולך is like זכי, since the agent seems to have acquired it for him.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"Deliver a מנה to so-and-so,"
and he went and looked for him and did not find him,
phrases.notes: The recipient had died, which is why his heirs come up later in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: it should go back to the sender.
If the sender died –
Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Yaakov said:
it should go back to the sender's heirs,
and some say:
to the heirs of the one it was sent to.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״הוֹלֵךְ מָנֶה לִפְלוֹנִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the suggestion in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים argue about whether הולך works like זכי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי נתן and רבי יעקב against the יש אומרים

steps.title: More opinions: honor the dead, split it, or let the agent decide
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: רבי מאיר says there is a מצוה to carry out the dead person's words. חכמים say to split the money. Others say the agent may do whatever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא said in the name of רבי יעקב, who said it in the name of רבי מאיר: It is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead. The חכמים say: They should split it. And here they said: Whatever the agent wants, he may do.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and lists more opinions about what to do with the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives a reason for sending the money to the recipient's side: honoring the dead sender's wishes. חכמים are unsure, so they split it between the two sides. A third view leaves the decision to the agent.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to carry out a dead person's instructions

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said in the name of Rabbi Yaakov,
who said it in the name of Rabbi Meir:
It is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead.
And the חכמים say: They should split it.
And here they said:
phrases.notes: "Here" means בבל, where the scholars had their own practice.

phrases.english: Whatever the agent wants, he may do.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more opinions.
steps.raayaObject: The range of opinions on where the money goes
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יעקב appears twice. In step 16 he says the money goes to the sender's heirs. Here, as quoted in רבי מאיר's name, the view sounds like it favors the recipient. Keep the two reports separate.

steps.title: רבי שמעון הנשיא's real case
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון הנשיא reports that this happened before him, and the ruling was to return the money to the sender's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון הנשיא said: A case like this happened through me, and they said: It should go back to the sender's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a real story where the money was given back to the sender's heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An actual ruling counts for a lot. Here, in practice, the recipient's side did not get the money, which fits the view that the recipient never acquired it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon HaNasi said:
A case like this happened through me,
and they said: It should go back to the sender's heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַנָּשִׂיא: עַל יָדִי הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא with a real ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an actual case, the money was returned to the heirs of the sender.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives many views: the sender's heirs, the recipient's heirs (מצוה לקיים דברי המת), split it, or the agent decides. The real case ruled for the sender's heirs. The גמרא will now check whether this argument is really about הולך and זכי.

steps.title: Mapping the first opinions onto whether 'deliver' means 'acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא and רבי נתן and רבי יעקב hold הולך is not like זכי, while the יש אומרים hold הולך is like זכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? The תנא קמא holds that 'deliver' is not like 'acquire.' רבי נתן and רבי יעקב also hold that 'deliver' is not like 'acquire,' and even though the sender died, we do not say it is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead. The יש אומרים hold that 'deliver' is like 'acquire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove its suggestion from Step 15 by showing which side of the הולך/זכי question each opinion in the ברייתא is on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הולך is not like זכי, the recipient never acquired the money, so it goes back to the sender or to his heirs. If הולך is like זכי, the recipient acquired it right away, so it goes to the recipient's heirs. That explains why the יש אומרים send it to the recipient's heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that...?' This is how the גמרא opens a suggested proof.
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
'Deliver.' The sender tells the agent to take the money to the recipient.
'Acquire.' The agent takes possession for the recipient right away.
It is a מצוה to carry out what a person who has died wanted done

phrases.english: What, is it not that they argue about this:
that the first tanna holds:
'Deliver' is not like 'acquire';
phrases.notes: So the money was never the recipient's, and it goes back to the sender.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Yaakov also hold
phrases.notes: These are the ones in the ברייתא who said the money goes to the sender's heirs.

phrases.english: 'deliver' is not like 'acquire',
and even though the sender died,
we do not say 'it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead';
and the 'some say' opinion holds that 'deliver' is like 'acquire';
phrases.notes: So the recipient owned the money right away, which is why it goes to his heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts reading the ברייתא from Steps 16-18 as a proof for the suggestion in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that whether הולך is like זכי is an argument among the תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the agent who could not find the recipient

steps.title: Placing רבי מאיר's opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds הולך is not like זכי, but once the sender has died, we carry out the dead person's wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא said in the name of רבי יעקב, who said it in the name of רבי מאיר: 'deliver' is not like 'acquire.' But when the sender has died, we say it is a מצוה to carry out the words of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues lining up the opinions. It explains that רבי מאיר agrees הולך is not like זכי, but he gives the money to the recipient because of the מצוה to honor a dead person's wishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees with רבי נתן and רבי יעקב on the basic rule. They argue only about whether the מצוה to carry out a dead person's words applies here. This shows how two opinions can share one view on הולך and still reach different results.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he died

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר –
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Yaakov, who said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from Step 17: 'רבי מאיר says there is a מצוה to carry out the dead person's words.'

phrases.english: 'deliver' is not like 'acquire',
however, where the sender died,
we say it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead;

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues mapping the opinions of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the תנאים argue about הולך and זכי
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's opinion in the ברייתא

steps.title: Placing the חכמים, the כאן אמרו group, and רבי שמעון הנשיא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים are unsure, so they split the money. The כאן אמרו group says the agent's judgment is better. רבי שמעון הנשיא is only reporting a real case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say to divide the money because they are unsure of the law. The ones who said 'here they said' hold that the agent's own judgment is better. רבי שמעון הנשיא came to teach us about an actual incident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes lining up the rest of the opinions. This completes its suggested proof that the ברייתא is a full argument about הולך and זכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not decide whether הולך is like זכי, so they split the money between the two sides. The כאן אמרו group also treats the case as uncertain, but they prefer to let the agent decide rather than divide. רבי שמעון הנשיא adds no new view; he tells us how a real case was decided.

keyTerms.meaning: The agent's own judgment about who should get the money

steps.whatToRemember: According to this suggestion, every opinion in the ברייתא depends on two questions: whether הולך is like זכי, and whether the מצוה to carry out a dead person's words applies here.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: They should divide it,
because they are unsure;
and the 'here they said' opinion holds that the agent's discretion is better;
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from Step 17 that the agent may do whatever he wants.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon HaNasi
came to teach us an incident.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יַחְלוֹקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the mapping that began in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the תנאים argue about הולך and זכי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The remaining opinions in the ברייתא

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the case is a dying giver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says no. With a healthy giver, everyone agrees. The ברייתא is about a שכיב מרע, and it follows the argument between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. With a healthy giver, everyone agrees. What case are we dealing with here? A person on his deathbed. They argue about the same thing that רבי אלעזר and the רבנן argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Steps 19-21. It explains the ברייתא in a different way, so the argument there is not about הולך and זכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the giver was healthy, everyone agrees that הולך is not like זכי. The ברייתא is about a שכיב מרע, a person on his deathbed, whose gifts may follow special rules. So the opinions are arguing about the dispute between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן, not about הולך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With what case are we dealing here?' The גמרא uses this to set the case in a specific situation.

steps.confusionAlert: Rejecting the proof does not mean הולך is like זכי. It only means this ברייתא cannot prove that the תנאים argue about it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sends the question back to where it was. No source has yet shown that the תנאים argue about הולך and זכי.

phrases.english: No; with a healthy person
everyone agrees;
phrases.notes: He means everyone agrees that with a healthy giver, 'deliver' is not like 'acquire.'

phrases.english: and with what are we dealing here?
With a person on his deathbed,
and they disagree in the dispute between Rabbi Elazar and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּבָרִיא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in Steps 19-21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that the ברייתא shows the תנאים argue about הולך and זכי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be explained as a case of a שכיב מרע, so the argument follows a different dispute and not הולך and זכי.

steps.title: The משנה: does a sick person's gift work by words alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי אלעזר says that for a healthy or a dangerously ill person, land is acquired through money, a document or taking possession, and movable items only through pulling. The חכמים say that for a sick person, both kinds are acquired through speech alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: someone gives out his property by speech alone. רבי אלעזר says: whether he is healthy or dangerously ill, land is acquired through money, a document, or taking possession. Movable items are acquired only through pulling. The חכמים say: for a sick person, both land and movable items are acquired through speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the source it mentioned in step 22, the משנה where רבי אלעזר and the חכמים argue about a sick person's gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר treats a מסוכן exactly like a healthy person, so his words alone do not transfer anything. He needs a real act of קנין. The חכמים say a sick person's speech alone is enough. This is the argument the ברייתא about the agent now depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: One who divides his property orally, by speech alone
A dangerously ill person, also called a שכיב מרע
Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land
Pulling, a way to acquire movable items
Taking possession, for example by working the land

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying a sick person can never give gifts. He is saying the sick person needs the same normal act of acquisition as a healthy person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument decides whether a dying sender's words alone already gave the money to the receiver. That is how the גמרא explains the different views in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: one who divides his property orally,
phrases.notes: בבא בתרא 156a

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
both a healthy person and a dangerously ill person:
property that serves as a guarantee
phrases.notes: This means land. A lender can collect from it, so it backs up a loan.

phrases.english: is acquired through money, a document, or taking possession,
and property that does not serve as a guarantee
is acquired only through pulling.
And the Rabbis say:
both this and that are acquired through speech.
phrases.notes: The חכמים are talking about the sick person here, not the healthy one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַמְחַלֵּק נְכָסָיו עַל פִּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה behind step 22's claim that the ברייתא follows the argument between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: a sick person's gift needs a regular קנין, the same as a healthy person's. חכמים: a sick person's gift works through speech alone.

steps.title: The חכמים begin a story about the mother of the בני רוכל
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי אלעזר by starting to tell about a real case: the mother of the בני רוכל was sick and said that something should be given. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: there was a case with the mother of the בני רוכל. She was sick, and she said: 'Let it be given…'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים start to bring a real case to challenge רבי אלעזר. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use a real event (a מעשה) as proof that a sick person's words alone work. Her instructions are about to be quoted, and then the חכמים will show how they were carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: A real event, brought as proof
The sons of Rokhel, a family name

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: The חכמים are speaking to רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: There was an incident with the mother of the sons of Rokhel
who was ill,
and she said: "Let it be given
phrases.notes: Her sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִמָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי רוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the quoted משנה, the חכמים challenge רבי אלעזר's view from step 23 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים's view that a sick person's gift works through speech alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case with the sick mother of the בני רוכל. Her instructions continue in the next section.
